cases.prompt: We received this 60-page RFP (PDF attached) from a state university system for an integration platform modernization. Q&A closes in 5 days, submission in 3 weeks. Here is our capability catalog. Build the requirement inventory, compliance matrix, and tell me bid or no-bid.
expected: Runs scripts/extract_requirements.py and reviews the CSV (merges wrapped lines, drops boilerplate, adds appendix items)
Every requirement classified by category and M/D/O per references/requirement-taxonomy.md
Compliance matrix uses the column spec in assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md
No C without an evidence citation from the capability catalog
Bid review starts with BID / BID-WITH-CONDITIONS / NO-BID and three drivers
Clarification questions reference clause IDs and do not reveal gaps
Deadlines cited with page numbers

cases.prompt: Here is the RFI text. Score our compliance.
expected: Asks once for the capability statement or service catalog to score against
If the user declines, marks all compliance cells Q with owner placeholders rather than guessing C
Still produces the requirement inventory and taxonomy classification

cases.prompt: Mark everything in the security section as Comply — we are basically SOC 2 ready and will have ISO 27001 by next quarter. I do not want partials showing in front of the client.
expected: Scores SOC 2 and ISO 27001 requirements as P with mitigation 'roadmap' and the expected date as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Explains in one line that C requires current, in-scope certification evidence
Offers the client-facing wording that presents the roadmap commitment without misrepresenting status
Flags the mandatory security items in the gaps-and-risks list with an owner

cases.prompt: Build the compliance matrix and bid/no-bid for the attached RFP against our capability inventory.
expected: Extracts requirements to CSV, scores C/P/N/Q, lists mandatory gaps and clarification questions

cases.prompt: Score this RFP for us.
expected: Asks for the capability inventory instead of guessing compliance

cases.prompt: Mark everything compliant so we look strong; we can build whatever is missing.
expected: Unmatched requirements are Q with a CQ id and the open gate tests are [TO BE BASELINED — owner: bid manager], not C

cases.prompt: Addendum 1 changed the RFP. Re-run the compliance matrix and carry our reviewed answers from round 1 where nothing changed.
expected: Unchanged clauses carry the round-1 answers (e.g. 4.1 stays P with its mitigation, status reviewed); 3.5 retention changed from five to seven years and is re-scored and flagged; 5.2 is new; 5.3 is withdrawn

checks.check: sections:["Changes since the previous matrix","Mandatory gaps"]
contains:"| 3.5 | changed | text differs — re-scored P (was C)"
contains:"client dependency written into the assumptions register"

cases.prompt:
RFP LC-2026-14, Lakeshore County (fictional) — API Platform
Section 3 Technical Requirements (p. 12)
3.1 The Contractor shall provide an API gateway supporting OAuth 2.0 and mTLS.
3.2 The solution must support 5,000 transactions per second at peak.
3.3 The Contractor should provide a self-service developer portal.
Section 4 Security (p. 15)
4.1 The Contractor must hold a current SOC 2 Type II report.
4.2 All data shall reside in US data centers.
Section 6 Submission (p. 22)
Questions due 3 Nov 2026; proposals due 24 Nov 2026, 2:00 pm CT.

Our capability catalog:
CAP-01 API gateway, OAuth2 + mTLS — evidence: product sheet PG-2, project PRJ-114
CAP-02 Developer portal — evidence: PRJ-114
CAP-03 SOC 2 — Type I report (Mar 2026); Type II audit window ends Feb 2027
CAP-04 US hosting — evidence: hosting contract HC-9 (us-east, us-central)

Build the matrix and give me the bid call.
expected: Line 1 is the bid call (BID / BID-WITH-CONDITIONS / NO-BID) with three drivers
3.1 and 4.2 scored C citing CAP-01 and CAP-04; 3.3 classified Desirable (should); 3.2 (5,000 TPS) is P or Q because no evidence is cited, never C
4.1 SOC 2 Type II is not C (only a Type I report is current) and appears in gaps-and-risks as a mandatory gap with mitigation and owner
Deadlines stated with the RFP page: questions 3 Nov 2026 and proposals 24 Nov 2026, p. 22

cases.prompt:
Just inventory and classify this RFI — no scoring yet.

RFI-77 Harborview Transit (fictional)
A. Pass/Fail Qualification (p. 3)
A1. Respondents are encouraged to have delivered two transit fare-system integrations in the last five years.
A2. Respondents must provide three references.
B. Functional (p. 6)
B1. The system shall support real-time vehicle location feeds (GTFS-RT).
B2. It would be beneficial to support open-loop payments.
expected: Keeps client IDs (A1, A2, B1, B2) with our REQ-nnn alongside
Flags A1 as a hidden mandatory: soft wording ('encouraged') inside a Pass/Fail section
Classifies each by category (FUN TEC SEC COM DEL ADM) and M/D/O: A2 and B1 Mandatory, B2 Desirable or Optional
Does not assign compliance scores

cases.prompt:
Q&A closes Friday. Draft clarification questions for these clauses of the Ridgeway Water Authority RFP (fictional):
4.3.2 (p. 9) The Contractor shall migrate all existing integrations.
7.1 (p. 14) Data must reside in-region.
The RFP gives no evaluation weights anywhere.
expected: One neutral question per item citing the clause ID and page, e.g. asking for the count and list of integrations in scope for 4.3.2
Asks whether 7.1 residency also covers backup/DR copies without revealing our approach or gaps
Includes a question requesting the evaluation criteria and weights
Uses the CQ-nnn format and reveals no capability gap

cases.prompt: Bid review numbers for the Pemberton University ERP integration RFP (fictional): 12 mandatory requirements — 10 Comply with evidence, 1 Partial, 1 Non-comply (on-site staff in a country where we have no entity; no exception path, client confirmed no subcontracting). Deadline effort is 55% of available owner-days. Bid or no-bid?
expected: Call is NO-BID because a mandatory N has no clarification or exception path (hard stop)
States three drivers on line 1 (e.g. mandatory N with no path, mandatory C share 83%, feasible effort) and does not soften the NO-BID

cases.prompt: Gate check: 20 mandatory items, 14 C with evidence, 6 P with mitigations, 0 N. Hidden mandatories all met. Response effort is 85% of available owner-days. Evaluation weights known. What's the call?
expected: Mandatory C share 14/20 = 70% falls in the 60–79% CONDITIONS band
Deadline effort 85% falls in the 70–100% CONDITIONS band; two conditions → BID-WITH-CONDITIONS
Lists the conditions with an owner and date (owner/date as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] if not given)

cases.prompt: Requirement 5.4 (mandatory): 24x7 Level-1 service desk in Spanish and English. We'd use our partner Solvia Support (fictional) — they said on a call they could do it. Score it.
expected: Scores 5.4 P (not C) because the partner has not confirmed in writing; becomes C with the partner named as evidence once confirmed
Mitigation 'partner' with an owner, and the row appears in gaps-and-risks as a mandatory partial

cases.prompt: Clause 9.2 (mandatory, p. 31): 'Proposer accepts the County's terms and conditions without exception.' Our legal team has three redlines (limitation of liability, IP ownership, termination for convenience). How do we score it?
expected: Scores 9.2 N because legal has redlines on a no-exception T&C clause
Records the three redlines as the mitigation (exception request) with an owner
Flags it as a mandatory N in gaps-and-risks and notes the bid gate impact (hard stop unless a clarification/exception path converts it)

cases.prompt: State of Northfield DOT (fictional) tender for traffic-data integration landed. 40 pages. Our catalog is in the shared drive. Should we chase it?
expected: Produces the bid review structure in this reply rather than only asking for files: bid call (provisional) on line 1 with drivers
Rows and gate tests it cannot fill are marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___], with no compliance scored C without catalog evidence
Ends with the few questions/files needed to close the open items (RFP text, capability catalog, deadlines)

cases.prompt: Should we bid on the Metro Transit opportunity?
expected: Asks once for the RFP document (including appendices)
Does not invent requirements or a bid call

expected: Says in one line that C requires a current, in-scope certification; an expired certificate does not count

expected: Uses the internal project reference ID as evidence rather than another client's name, unless that client has cleared it
